contents.title: Anarchy, State, and Utopia
contents.content: Robert Nozick, 1974. Individuals have rights, and only a minimal state limited to protection against force, theft and fraud is justified. The entitlement theory of justice: a holding is just if it was acquired and transferred justly, whatever pattern of distribution results. The Wilt Chamberlain argument against patterned principles such as the difference principle.

contents.title: Second Treatise of Government
contents.description: John Locke, 1689. Natural rights to life, liberty and property; property begins when a person mixes their labour with the world. Government by consent, limited to protecting those rights.

contents.title: The Constitution of Liberty
contents.content: Friedrich Hayek, 1960. Liberty as the absence of coercion under general rules of law. The knowledge needed to plan a society is dispersed among individuals, so the state should protect a framework and not aim at a distribution.

contents.title: The Road to Serfdom
contents.content: Friedrich Hayek, 1944. Central economic planning concentrates power and erodes individual liberty and the rule of law.

contents.title: A Theory of Justice
contents.content: John Rawls, 1971. Read to know the case being answered: the original position, the veil of ignorance, the difference principle and justice as fairness.

contents.title: The Machinery of Freedom
contents.content: David Friedman, 1973. A consequentialist case for private property and markets in place of the state, including law and protection.
